chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mihazyar, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) wrote to a man in his own handwriting, and I read it containing a supplication to be said: 'O He Who existed before everything, then created everything, then remains while everything perishes; and O He Who is not in the highest heavens, nor in the lowest earths, nor above them, nor between them, nor below them, is a god besides Him [to be worshipped].'
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for Divine Unity written by Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This supplication, transmitted through the chain of Shaykh al-Saduq, exemplifies the Shia theological emphasis on *Tawhid al-Sifat* by negating spatial containment (*Tanzih*) while affirming eternal pre-existence. It reflects the scholarly tradition of using precise linguistic negation to distinguish God from created entities, reinforcing the concept that the Divine is not limited by the physical dimensions of the universe.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 11. Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) said on the authority of Muhammad ibn Yahya al- `Attar on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of `Abd Allah ibn Muhammad, on the authority of `Ali ibn Mihazyar

that Abu Ja`far al-Baqir (AS) wrote a letter to a man in his own handwriting. I read the supplication it contained, and it said: O He Who existed before anything existed! O He Who created everything! O He Who will remain after everything perishes! O He besides Whom there is no god! O He Who is served in the highest of the heaves! O He Who is served in the lowest of the Earths! And O He Who is served between them, and below them!
